subject: Latency pledge and POC parameters — hosted vs current vendor
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@loombio.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-25T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: latency pledge and POC parameters

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on acceptance criteria for the p95/p99 end-to-end latency POC comparing Redwood hosted vs your current provider.

High-level summary from LoomBio today (as discussed):
- Current production envelope (sampled): p95 ~ 620 ms, p99 ~ 2.3 s across mixed text-gen & streaming chat traffic.
- Peak concurrency: 180 active concurrent streams, typical sustained concurrency ~60.
- Traffic mix: 65% short requests (< 128 tokens), 25% medium (128-512), 10% long (>512).
- Streaming usage: yes — optimistic early-utterance latency matters.

Redwood hosted target (what we propose to demonstrate in the POC):
- p95 end-to-end < 300 ms (API response with streaming first-byte latency measured)
- p99 end-to-end < 800 ms for typical short/medium requests
- Maintain sustained concurrency to 200 streams during load slices with automatic batching + KV cache enabled
- Graceful tail handling: automated fallback to quantized variant if sustained burst > configured capacity

What we need from you to scope the POC:
1) Representative traffic trace (5000-10,000 requests) or a CSV with timestamp, request size (tokens), and streaming flag — we can ingest this into our harness to replay realistic traffic (attachment request: traffic-envelope.csv).
2) Example prompt templates (a few dozen) that reflect real best-effort paths for short vs long flows.
3) Confirmation on region preference (us-west vs us-east) — you mentioned us-west earlier.
4) Security checklist items: do you need SOC2 report or IP allowlist pre-negotiation before we provision test keys?

Proposed POC plan:
- Redwood provisions a sandbox tenant + short-lived API key for LoomBio (shared via secure link).
- Week 0: ingest traffic envelope & templates; run warm-up trace to validate sequence lengths and KV cache hit assumptions.
- Week 1: two controlled load windows (2 x 60-minute slices): baseline (incumbent replay) and Redwood-hosted run. We collect p50/p95/p99, streaming first-byte latency, and throughput.
- Acceptance: p95 improvement >= 20% vs incumbent and p99 < 800 ms for short/medium flows, plus no functional regressions.

Attachments: call recording (call-recording.mp4), suggested CSV header for traffic-envelope.csv.

Next steps / immediate asks: can you share the traffic CSV and two representative prompt templates by Tue (2028-04-30)? If yes, I’ll schedule the sandbox + runbook and loop Marissa to own the harness.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.com | M: +1-415-555-0123

From: Samir Patel <samir@loombio.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Raman <asha@loombio.com>
Date: 2028-04-25T18:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency pledge and POC parameters

Evelyn — appreciate the crisp recap. Confirming a few clarifications and constraints from our side: 

1) Traffic data: we can export a 7k-request sample (timestamp, tokens, streaming flag). I’ll attach the export to a secure link — expect it by EOD tomorrow.
2) Current provider baseline you quoted is correct in general; numbers vary by time of day. For the POC we’d like you to run both our production replay window (weekday peak) and a synthetic stress window (short bursts at 2x peak).
3) Streaming note: our UX is particularly sensitive to first-byte for streaming responses — we need explicit first-byte latency graphs and a breakdown of any prefix caching behavior you use.
4) Security: SOC2 is required before we move to any long-lived keys. Short-lived sandbox keys (1–2 weeks) are ok for the POC provided they are delivered through a signed internal support ticket.

Availability for the POC windows: we prefer May 13–17 (PST). Please confirm if Redwood can reserve two 60-minute windows within that range.

Asha (cc) will coordinate the traffic export and share the sample link.

Best,
Samir
CTO — LoomBio
samir@loombio.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-26T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency pledge and POC parameters — technical follow-up

Hi Samir / Evelyn — Marissa here (SE) — jumping in with the POC harness plan and a few technical asks so we can turn the traffic sample into actionable load slices.

Technical plan (short):
- We’ll convert your CSV into three replay traffic profiles: peak-replay, steady-sustain (60m at nominal), and burst-stress (5m spikes at 2x).
- For streaming, we measure: connect latency, first-byte streaming latency, and end-to-end token throughput.
- We’ll run the Redwood hosted job with: KV prefix cache enabled, batching window tuned to preserve latency SLOs, and two model variants (full fp16 and 4-bit quantized) to observe tail behavior.

Questions / inputs needed from LoomBio:
- Confirm tokenization method (our token counts must match your counts). Do you use GPT-like BPE?
- Any per-request timeout thresholds in your client (we need these to align the POC load harness).
- Are there end-to-end headers or middleware latencies you want included (e.g., internal proxy adds 40–60 ms)? If so please provide a sample header log.

I’ve attached the POC harness instructions (poc-harness-instructions.md) — it includes the CSV template we need, how to annotate streaming turns, and the JSON schema for the results we’ll publish back.

Proposed quick timeline:
- 4/30: LoomBio shares traffic CSV + tokenization note
- 5/6: Redwood publishes sandbox & runbook; sync call to align on exact windows
- 5/13–17: POC windows (two 60m runs) as Samir requested

Happy to pair on the data export with Asha.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: latency pledge and POC parameters — confirmed windows & action items

Thanks Samir — great, we’ll proceed as proposed. Final confirmations and action list: 

Confirmed POC windows: May 14, 2028 — 10:00–11:00 PST (baseline replay) and May 16, 2028 — 14:00–15:00 PST (hosted run). Please flag if these collide with your internal calendar.

Action items (owner / due):
- LoomBio: export traffic CSV + tokenization note (Asha) — due 2028-04-30 — await Drive link.
- Redwood: provision sandbox tenant + short-lived API key; publish runbook (Marissa) — due 2028-05-06 — runbook link will be posted to the HubSpot deal.
- LoomBio: provide any proxy/middleware latency documentation (Samir) — due 2028-05-06.
- Redwood/SE: run pre-warm and validate token counts (Marissa) — due 2028-05-09.
- Both: joint sync 30-minute call week of 2028-05-06 to confirm windows and observability hooks (Evelyn to schedule).

Delivery expectations: we will provide per-window artifacts: p50/p95/p99 latencies, first-byte streaming CDF, throughput curves, and a short incident log if any fallbacks occurred. Acceptance criteria reiterated: p95 improvement >= 20% vs incumbent and p99 < 800 ms for short/medium flows.

Security note: we will transmit sandbox keys via the Redwood support ticket system and provide our SOC2 summary if needed.

Thanks all — I’ll create the HubSpot meeting and attach the runbook once Marissa confirms the sandbox details.

—
